# Context: elementwise-ops (arith, div_rem, exp_log, trig, rounding, min_max, cmp, bitwise, bit_count, float_special, complex, select, cast, transmute, sub_dtype)

Short paths: bare names are in `jix/src/ops/elementwise/`, except `simd.rs`, `traits_util.rs`,
`bool.rs` (jix/src/scalar/), `error.rs`, `dtype.rs`, `context.rs` (jix/src/), `buf.rs`,
`core_trait.rs`, `index.rs` (jix/src/storage/), `test_util.rs` (jix/src/util/). `ops/` is
jix/src/ops/; `casting.rs` and "jix-py div_rem.rs" are in jix-py/src/ops/elementwise/.

## Purpose

The concrete element-wise ops and their per-element kernels. Most ops are a `define_op1!` /
`define_op2!` wrapper (op1.rs:166-261, op2.rs:229-332, owned by the pipeline subsystem) around
`Op1<S,K>` / `Op2<S1,S2,K>` whose zero-sized kernel calls a public scalar trait re-exported as
`jix::scalar::*` (e.g. `Div::div(a, b, &mut status)` + `div_bulk`). The traits and impls are
generated by `jix/src/scalar/traits_util.rs`; SIMD bodies go through `jix/src/scalar/simd.rs` on
`fearless_simd` 1.1.0. Execution is the fused pipeline (pipeline.rs). Hand-written storages here:
`Clamp` (min_max.rs:191-377), `Select` (select.rs:37-433, own strided loops), `ApproxEq`
(cmp.rs:594-672), swapped `Greater`/`GreaterEqual` (cmp.rs:330-478), `Cast` (cast.rs:412-468),
`Real`/`Imaginary` (complex.rs), `SubDtype` (ops/sub_dtype.rs), `Transmute` (ops/transmute.rs).

## Contracts

Provided:
- P1. `f_bulk(xs)[i] == f(xs[i])` (modulo NaN payload) with the same OR'ed status. The trait default
  bulk loops the scalar fn (traits_util.rs:21-33, 157-173); SIMD only where an impl gives
  `fn f_bulk = |v| ...` (traits_util.rs:106-121, 263-306). `map_vectors*` fall back to scalar when
  N is not a multiple of the vector chunk (simd.rs:184-186, 226-231); bool-output SIMD runs only on
  AVX2 with N a multiple of the u8 lanes (simd.rs:338-340); casts gate on `only_on` (cast.rs:89-93).
- P2. Kernels never panic on data. Only integer kernels report: they write a fallback (0) and OR an
  `ArithmeticErrorKind` (jix/src/error.rs:314-327: `DivideByZero`, `NegativePower`). Float kernels
  never set a status (error.rs:317-317). The pipeline ORs per-chunk status and returns
  `status.into_result()` only after the whole output is written (pipeline.rs:245-310, contract
  text pipeline.rs:50-50), so a failed push read leaves fallback values in `out`. Any error fails
  the read; there is no errstate/mode any more (removed in #95).
- P3. Output dtype is `K::Output::DTYPE`; zero-size output dtypes rejected (op1.rs:34, op2.rs:39,
  ops/sub_dtype.rs:60); `shape * output itemsize` overflow rejected at construction (op1.rs:35,
  op2.rs:52), which covers widening Cast/cmp/Pow. Clamp/Select/SubDtype/Transmute never widen.
- P4. Shapes must be exactly equal, no broadcasting in Rust: Op2 (op2.rs:41-51), Clamp
  (min_max.rs:207-214), Select (select.rs:65-73). jix-py broadcasts first (0-stride views).
  Operators / `Array::<op>()` methods `unwrap()` with `#[track_caller]` and panic on mismatch.
- P5. No implicit promotion; an op exists only for the implemented (lhs, rhs) pairs. Same-type:
  Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Divide*/Remainder*/Equal/NotEqual/Less/LessEqual/Maximum/Minimum/BitAnd/Or/Xor.
  Mixed: Pow int x {u8,u16,u32} (arith.rs:321-325), int x {i8,i16,i32,i64} (335-356), f32|f64 x
  {i8,u8,i16,u16,i32} (357-368), f32|f64 x f32 (369-373), f64 x f64 (374-378), f16 x
  {i8,u8,i16,u16,i32} and f16 x f16 (379-401); Shl/Shr any int x any int, output = lhs type
  (bitwise.rs:94-122, 171-177); Rotate int x u32 (bitwise.rs:144-153); cmp also u64 x i64 and i64 x
  u64 (cmp.rs:43-54). Greater/GreaterEqual = Less/LessEqual on swapped operands (cmp.rs:348).
- P6. Select: numpy.where semantics, condition dtype `bool8` (select.rs:52-57), `x.dtype() ==
  y.dtype()` runtime-checked (61-67), any dtype incl. structs. Transmute: ONLY itemsize is checked
  (transmute.rs:49-53). SubDtype: pull returns the parent buffer shifted by the field offset with
  the PARENT strides (ops/sub_dtype.rs:96-99); push copies field bytes with NdCopier (101-119).
- P7. Op1/Op2/Clamp/Select read through `context.read_cached` with their own `ArrayCacheId`
  (op1.rs:65, op2.rs:120, min_max.rs:271, select.rs:327; jix/src/context.rs:148-236). SubDtype
  and Transmute have no id of their own and read their inner directly. Cast, Real/Imaginary,
  ApproxEq and the define_op* ops are Op1/Op2 underneath, so they get P7 through them.

Relied on:

  Sound only because Dtype equality implies identical layout, i.e. on the `unsafe trait Dtyped`

- R2. `read_bulk` safety (pipeline.rs:51-60): `to_buf` (pipeline.rs:245-310, 595-648) guarantees

- R3. A child's pull `read_data` returns a buffer valid for the whole region, one stride per dim

- R4. An `Index` is never empty (core_trait.rs:84; sizes are `NonZeroUsize`, jix/src/storage/index.rs:16-19);

Unsafe-fn preconditions and who establishes them:
- [CHANGED #105] `Transmute::new` / `new_array`, `Array::transmute_elements` / `_dyn` are now SAFE
  fns (main a7b0656, "make Transmute safe"); before #105 they were `unsafe` with the CALLER
  guaranteeing every element is a valid bit pattern of the new dtype. Soundness now rests entirely
  on the `Dtyped` contract. Every `Dtyped` type accepts all bit patterns and has no padding (dtype.rs:1158-1160; `bool`
  is not Dtyped, `bool8` is), so this reduces to "the source bytes are initialized", which every
  storage provides. The `_elements` methods panic (unwrap) on itemsize mismatch (documented).
- `read_bulk` (pub(crate) trait method): established by pipeline `to_buf` (R2).
- `OperandTyped::new_input` (pipeline.rs:812-818): established by `check_dtype` in the default leaf
  (core_trait.rs:122-124) - Transmute and SubDtype use that default leaf.
- `StridedBuf::with_offset` (buf.rs:289-316): caller ensures the shifted view is valid (SubDtype, R4+R5).
- Select's private `inner_loop` / `inner_loop_generic` (select.rs:215, 286): `len` elements at the
  given strides in bounds of out, y and cond; out distinct from y/cond; `itemsize == size_of::<T>()`
  (hard assert select.rs:229).

## Unsafe inventory

- min_max.rs:329-343 (ClampPipeline::read_bulk): forwards read_bulk (R2) + `transmute_copy` (R1),
  check_dtype at min_max.rs:286. Same pattern in op1.rs:111-119 / op2.rs:174-180 used by every
  Op1/Op2-based op here (define_op* ops, Cast, Real, ApproxEq). Non-local: Dtyped impl correctness.
- select.rs:167-212: table of `unsafe fn` loops, called per inner run with NdIterUnordered offsets
  over out (fresh pool buffer from `OutBuf::materialize`, or the caller's push buffer checked by
  check_out_buf at 136), `y_view` and `condition_view` (pull views, R3). In-bounds relies on R3+R6
  (non-local). Loop choice by (itemsize, alignment) at 185-194; `aligned` (161-166) is trivially true
  when !REQUIRE_ALIGNED; contiguity is only debug_asserted (227-229).
- select.rs:234-279 typed loop: reads `[T; LANES]` / `[bool8; LANES]` and writes back into x/out with
  `read_maybe_aligned` / `write_maybe_aligned`. bool8 has no invalid bytes.
- select.rs:296-305 generic loop: `copy_from_nonoverlapping(y -> out, itemsize)` where !cond.
  Distinctness: out is a fresh pool buffer or the caller's exclusive `&mut`; Python `numpy(out=)`
  overlapping an input is K31 (intended, documented).
- select.rs:378-391 pipeline read_bulk: forwards, condition read as bool8 via `bool::from`.
- ops/sub_dtype.rs:97-99 `with_offset`: slicing is bounds-checked (Slice variants in with_offset,
  pool/shared variants in `data()`, buf.rs:207-216), so a bad offset panics, not UB. Validity of the
  shifted view at the parent strides relies on R5 (non-local).
- ops/sub_dtype.rs:105 `get_unchecked(offset..)`: UB if offset > len. Established only by R4 (the
  parent pull holds element 0 at byte 0, >= parent itemsize > offset bytes); `debug_assert` at 103.
- ops/sub_dtype.rs:108-118 `NdCopier::copy` with parent strides, out strides, field dtype (same dtype
  as `NdCopier::new`, K54 fixed). Source span = last offset + field size <= parent bytes - offset (R3, R5).
- ops/transmute.rs: no unsafe at all since #105 (safe API; read_data forwards).
- None in arith, div_rem, exp_log, trig, rounding, cmp, bitwise, bit_count, float_special, complex,
  cast (outside the shared Op1/Op2 nodes).

## Edge-case surface

Integers:
- Add/Sub/Mul/Square/Neg/Abs wrap with NO status (arith.rs:82-87, 133-143, 194-199, 264-274); SIMD
  bodies use fearless_simd ops that also wrap (R8). i8 Mul/Square are scalar only (arith.rs:133-137, 312).
- Div/DivideTrunc/Floor/Euclid: b == 0 -> 0 + DivideByZero; MIN / -1 -> MIN with NO error
  (`int_quotient` div_rem.rs:292-313 returns `a`). Remainder*: b == 0 -> 0 + DivideByZero;
  MIN % -1 -> 0, no error (`int_remainder` 316-331). No SIMD bodies for integer division.
  Signed floor/euclid adjustments use non-wrapping `+`/`-` (div_rem.rs:236, 254, 276) - believed
  unreachable overflow (|rem| < |b|, adjusted quotient never at MIN), worth a proof.
- Pow: b < 0 -> 0 + NegativePower even for base 1/-1 (arith.rs:329-333); i64 b > u32::MAX via
  square-and-multiply (344-352); u8/u16/u32 exponents via `b as u32`.
- Shifts: `shift_count` reinterprets negative counts unsigned -> >= 128 > every width
  (bitwise.rs:173-191) -> 0, or -1 for negative signed Shr. SIMD i32 Shr clamps count to 31
  (110-115); u32 Shr selects 0 for counts >= 32 (116-125). Rotates take the count mod width.
- Mixed u64/i64 comparisons use exact formulas (cmp.rs:97-98, 119-120, 140-141, 156-157), no f64.
Floats (f32/f64):
- NaN: Maximum/Minimum -> canonical `Self::NAN` (min_max.rs:38-45, 103-110); comparisons false (`!=`
  true); ApproxEq false; cast to int -> 0; cast to bool8 -> TRUE; Sign(NaN) = NaN.
- Signed zero: Sign(+-0) = +0 (arith.rs:41-45); Max/Min of +-0 may return either; div quotients take
  `copysign(d)` (div_rem.rs:407); RemainderFloor zero result takes b's sign (440, SIMD 517); -0.0
  casts to bool8 FALSE (`!= 0`, SIMD `simd_ne(zero)` cast.rs:144).
- Rounded division specials (div_rem.rs:399-408): x/0 -> +-inf, 0/0 NaN, inf dividend with b != 0 ->
  NaN quotient, inf/0 -> inf; remainders: zero divisor or inf dividend -> NaN; b = inf -> rem = a.
  Past EXACT_LIMIT (2^24 f32, 2^53 f64; div_rem.rs:585, 593) `rem_trunc` switches to `a % b`
  (421, SIMD 487-489 + cold `fmod_past_limit` 493-502) while `div_floor` / `div_euclid` still use the
  inexact residual of `div_rem_trunc` (428-429, 448-450).
- Float Pow: exponent 0 -> 1.0 (NaN base too), 1 -> a, 2 -> a*a, i32 exponent computed in f64
  (arith.rs:348-359); otherwise `powf`. No status.
f16 (feature `half`): + - * / square and the div family are computed in f32 and rounded once
  (arith.rs:138-147, 275-282; div_rem.rs:345-359, 596-613) - correctly rounded, not a double-rounding
  bug; on aarch64+fp16 the native ops are used (arith.rs:148-153, 283-288; div_rem.rs:350-351), same
  results. Unary float ops via `f16::from_f32(x.to_f32().f())` (traits_util.rs:322-327). No f16 SIMD.
  Casts into f16: ints/f32 via `from_f32(x as f32)` (cast.rs:70, exact in f16's finite range), f64
  via `f16::from_f64` (cast.rs:54, K71 open). f16 ** i32 goes f64 -> f32 -> f16 (arith.rs:380, 392).
Complex (feature `num-complex`): only Complex<f32>/<f64> are Dtyped (dtype.rs:1200-1202), so the
  Complex<f16> impls (arith.rs:160-165, 212-217, 295-300; div_rem.rs:366-371; cmp.rs:76-82;
  cast.rs:301-302, 319-320) are unreachable from Array ops. Div is num_complex's textbook formula, no
  status (div_rem.rs:360-365, K27 intended). Abs uses hypot, real output (arith.rs:94-107). Complex
  -> bool8 is `!= 0+0i` (cast.rs:306-315); complex cannot cast to real. ApproxEq per component.
bool8: any non-zero byte is true (jix/src/scalar/bool.rs:8-22). And/Or/Xor/Not/cmp go through
  `bool::from` (bool.rs:37-100) and output canonical bytes; Maximum/Minimum use `std::cmp::max/min`
  on truthiness and return an OPERAND (min_max.rs:31-35, 96-100), so the output byte may be
  non-canonical (valid). Cast bool8 -> X gives 0/1 (cast.rs:63); Select tests `bool::from(cond)`.
Struct dtypes / inner shape: only Select, Transmute and SubDtype accept them. Select's typed loops
  cover (itemsize, align) in {(1,1),(2,2),(4,2),(4,4),(8,4),(8,8),(16,8|16)} (select.rs:183-192),
  else a byte-copy loop. SubDtype rejects parents with an inner shape (ops/sub_dtype.rs:45-49) and
  zero-size fields (61); the field may have an inner shape. Select has no zero-itemsize check.
Empty / 0-d / strides: read_data never sees an empty region (R4); a 0-d index is one element. 0-stride
  inputs are fine (pipeline stages them; Select takes the non-contiguous or generic loop); a push
  `out` cannot have aliasing strides (R9); length-1 dims may have any stride.
32-bit (x86, armv7 wheels): region size is bounded by `check_region_size` (error.rs:298-312) via
  check_out_buf in Op1/Op2/Clamp/Select/SubDtype; Transmute forwards to the inner's check.
SIMD/scalar split - the same element can go through either path: contiguous runs use the runtime
  level with LANES = 4|8 vectors' worth; strided runs use the compile-time baseline (SSE2 on x86_64)
  with LANES <= 4; the tail of every run is N=1 scalar (pipeline.rs:595-700). Any SIMD/scalar
  disagreement shows up as position-, length-, stride- or CPU-dependent results.

## Intentional behaviors

- Integer errors always fail the read (DivideByZero, NegativePower); float ops never report, their
  inf/NaN carry it (error.rs:314-327; jix-py/python/tests/test_arithmetic_errors.py:1-5, 59-71;
  K126/K145 "intended since #95"). There is no errstate.
- Integer wrap everywhere, also MIN / -1 -> MIN with no error (div_rem.rs:17, 33, 56-60;
  error.rs:319) and MIN % -1 -> 0 (div_rem.rs:131, 147); abs/neg/square/add/sub/mul/pow wrap
  (arith.rs:67-68, 120, 176-177, 222, 319). Abs/Neg exist only for signed ints.
- Pow: negative int exponent -> 0 + NegativePower like numpy's ValueError (arith.rs:315-315); float
  Pow uses powf with the f64 path for i32 exponents (K51/K144 fixed).
- Float DivideTrunc/Floor/Euclid use the EXACT quotient (`1.0 // 0.1 == 9`), an infinite dividend
  gives NaN like numpy's floor_divide, exact below 2^53 (2^24) and within one ulp above; "floor"
  differs from numpy beyond 2^51 (2^22) where numpy is off by one (div_rem.rs:33-36, 387-396;
  jix-py/src/ops/elementwise/div_rem.rs:33-40). RemainderTrunc = fmod; RemainderFloor = CPython
  float `%` (zero takes b's sign, div_rem.rs:171-172). Python `divide`/`remainder(rounding_mode=)`
  map to these structs (jix-py div_rem.rs:77-108); true division of ints promotes to f64 there.
- Round is half-away-from-zero, not numpy's half-to-even (rounding.rs:27-27). Sign(+-0.0) = 0.0
  (arith.rs:24-24). Floor/Ceil/Round exist only for floats.
- Maximum/Minimum propagate NaN as the canonical NaN, either zero may be returned
  (min_max.rs:18-19). Clamp = minimum(maximum(a, lo), hi), so lo > hi gives hi (min_max.rs:168-169).
- ApproxEq is NOT numpy.isclose: `|a-b| <= max(atol, rtol*max(|a|,|b|))`, same-sign infs equal,
  NaN never (cmp.rs:163-167, 228-234, 557-560); `jix.isclose` uses it (jix-py/src/ops/elementwise/cmp.rs:330).
- Shifts by >= width or negative -> 0 / -1 (bitwise.rs:86-88, 163-165); rotates mod width (132, 143).
- Casts follow Rust `as`: float -> int saturates, NaN -> 0; int -> int truncates/wraps; X -> bool8 is
  `!= 0` (NaN true); bool8 -> 0/1. Casts never set a status (cast.rs:414-434). i64/u64 -> f32 SIMD is
  deliberately disabled (cast.rs:224, 257). jix-py casts same-size int <-> int by Transmute
  (jix-py/src/ops/elementwise/casting.rs:63-66), bit-identical to `as`.
- f64 -> f16 uses `half::f16::from_f64` (cast.rs:54): K71 is open - do not re-report.
- Complex division is the unscaled textbook formula (K27 intended). `x ** 2` routes to Square in
  jix-py (K60 intended). Transmute checks only itemsize; alignment may differ (transmute.rs:10-10).
- Select evaluates BOTH branches for every element (select.rs:138-142, 386-392): an error in the
  unselected branch (int `select(b != 0, a // b, 0)`) still fails the read. Eager like numpy;
  undocumented - treat as design unless you find docs saying otherwise.
- Doc nits, not bugs: SwapBytes says i8/u8 unsupported (bit_count.rs:105-105) but they are
  implemented (51-56); `fixed_lhs_type` actually fixes the RHS item type (op2.rs:348-358, used at
  bitwise.rs:470-470); Cast struct docs list only Complex<f32>/<f64> (cast.rs:384). (#105 rewrote Transmute's
  docs, so the old `bool` Safety text is gone.)

## Hot spots

NEW/CHANGED since 6dbeb15 (#95 errstate removal, #96 where -> select, #97/#98 file split, #100
read cache, #103 `Index`, #104 `OutBuf`). The op1.rs/op2.rs split into these files is mostly a move;
the semantic changes are marked:
- [CHANGED #95] div_rem.rs:292-330: `int_quotient` dropped the Overflow flag (MIN / -1 now silent
  wrap); `int_remainder` unchanged. Is every non-zero-divisor `None` from checked_div /
  checked_rem / checked_rem_euclid really MIN / -1? Is the per-element DivideByZero flag set in both
  the bulk and the N=1 tail (Python test test_arithmetic_errors.py:59-71 covers both)?
- [CHANGED #95] arith.rs:326-347: Pow now flags `NegativePower`; float Pow, Div and the float div
  family lost their error classification (old `float_div_error` / `quotient_v` gone) but still run
  through `map_vectors2_status` with an unused status (div_rem.rs:537-578, traits_util.rs:284-306).
  Unary float kernels are plain `float_op1!` (traits_util.rs:310-344); #92's f16 overflow report is
  gone by design.
- [NEW #100] read cache: Select (select.rs:320-330) runs `check_out_buf` INSIDE the uncached closure
  (select.rs:134), so a cache hit skips `check_get_range` (context.rs:181-191 only re-checks a push
  out). Clamp/Op1/Op2 check before `read_cached`. Can a hit ever serve a region that would fail the
  checks, or a push `out` of a different dtype/itemsize?
- [CHANGED #100/#104] Select::read_data_uncached (select.rs:128-309): pulls cond and y, THEN
  materializes out and pushes x into it, then mixes in place. Three differently laid out buffers,
  0-stride y/cond, push out with caller strides, `read_layout_order` of the materialized out, the
  typed-loop table vs struct dtypes with itemsize != alignment; could the x push (or its cache
  eviction, context.rs:195-200) invalidate the live y/cond views when x, y, cond share storage?
- [CHANGED #104] SubDtype (ops/sub_dtype.rs:85-122): explicit empty paths are gone, push relies on
  R4 for `get_unchecked`; pull hands out `with_offset` of the parent buffer, which may be a writable
  PoolBufMut or a Shared cache buffer, at the parent strides - is it valid for every consumer that
  assumes only R3 (e.g. reused as a later push `out`, or a pipeline leaf with REQUIRE_ALIGNED)?
- [CHANGED #104] Transmute::read_data forwards the OutBuf (transmute.rs:74-82): the inner checks the
  push out with its own itemsize (equal) - and the pull bytes are reinterpreted with a possibly
  larger alignment (staging, pipeline.rs:471-483). `element_type_change` re-validates (113-120).
- [CHANGED #95, cross] jix-py same-size int <-> int cast by transmute (casting.rs:63-66): bool8 and
  f16 are excluded by `is_integer` (jix/src/dtype.rs:974); results must equal `Cast`'s `as`.
Unchanged but central:
- SIMD vs scalar equality: most SIMD tests compare with `same_value` (jix/src/util/test_util.rs:1378-1380),
  so -0.0 == +0.0 passes; only the float div family (div_rem.rs:926-983) and Maximum/Minimum NaN bits
  (min_max.rs:469) are bit-exact. Test inputs are 64 values: edge cases plus small ordinary values
  (test_util.rs:1342-1374) - no mid-range values (200.0 -> u8, 40000.0 -> u16). Only the host's
  levels run (K151); concrete array tests are tiny and hit only the scalar tail.
- Float div/rem past EXACT_LIMIT: can `divide_floor*b + remainder_floor == a` or the sign rules break
  between the residual-based quotient and the fmod-based remainder? Does `div_rem_trunc_v` agree with
  the scalar for b = +-0, a = +-inf, NaN, subnormals and quotients that overflow to inf?
- Cast step chains (cast.rs:195-282): KT/KU vector counts, widen order (cast.rs:345-372), sign
  extension (i8 -> u16), saturating chains for f32 -> i8/u8 and f64 -> i8..u32, and `only_on` lists vs
  the levels where the fearless_simd op is correct.
- Shr SIMD (bitwise.rs:107-122): i32 rhs bitcast then `min(31)`; u32 rhs `select`; does every
  (lhs, rhs) signedness pair match `unbounded_shr(shift_count(b))`?
- Bool-output SIMD (simd.rs:96-138, 325-359): mask narrowing order for 16/32/64-bit lanes on AVX2.
- define_swapped_cmp (cmp.rs:330-416): Op2 built as (b, a) with `swapped_operand_order`; spec based
  on the original first operand (402-409). Errors/messages and read order with mixed u64/i64.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- [RULED OUT in batch7-4: numpy 2.x's scalar fast path gives the same results] jix-py/src/ops/elementwise/arith.rs:549-550 (cross-subsystem): `jix.power(x, 0.5)` routes to Sqrt:
  x = -inf gives NaN where powf and np.power give +inf, and x = -0.0 gives -0.0 vs +0.0.
- [CONFIRMED in batch7-4, judged intended as K171] arith.rs:380, 392 (low): f16 ** i32 rounds the f64 powf result to f32 and then to f16, the
  double-rounding pattern K28 fixed for casts (possible 1-ulp f16 misrounding at ties).
